dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Kevin.
Hi Kevin, Dominic Iannuccilli. I know it's Saturday and City Hall's closed, so I figured I'd try the storm line and bother somebody who's already having a bad day.
No, that's what the line's for. What's going on?

So I manage a house at 50 Kingston Avenue, up on the Hill. There's a catch basin at the corner, and it's packed solid with leaves. Nobody cleared it all fall. With this nor'easter coming through today, the water has nowhere to go.
Okay, 50 Kingston Avenue, catch basin at the corner clogged with leaves. Where's the water ending up?

Backing right into the driveway. It's a couple inches deep now and it's running downhill toward the neighbor's garage. I'd say it's maybe ten feet from the door. I'm out here in a rain jacket that's clearly lying to me about being waterproof.
Yeah, those jackets are optimists. Is the water getting into the garage yet, or the house you manage?

Not yet in either one. The house is okay for now. The neighbor's garage is the worry, it's a little lower than my driveway. So who do I call to get somebody to look at this? Is that you, or is there another number?
That's us, you got the right place. I'm putting it in as a clogged catch basin with water flowing toward a neighboring garage. Can you give me the cross street?

Hang on, let me look at the sign. [pause] Sorry, the rain's got it all blurry. It's the corner right by my driveway, the one downhill. I don't remember the cross street offhand. I'm sixty-something, my memory's mostly for old baseball scores.
That's fine, the house number and the corner description will do it. Is anyone in danger, or is it just the water at this point?

Just the water so far. But it's been raining since this morning and it's only getting worse, and this basin has been like that for weeks. I'd have called sooner if I'd known anybody wanted to hear about it.
Understood. Crews are stretched thin during a storm like this, so I can't give you a time. But I'll flag it as water heading toward a structure, which bumps it up the list.
Okay. That's all I can ask, I guess. It's just that every time it rains hard there's a puddle there, and now it's a pond. Somebody should've cleaned that out.
I hear you. Can I get a callback number in case the crew needs to reach you?
Sure, it's 401-555-0156. That's the landline, so if I don't pick up I'm probably out in the driveway with a push broom.
Got it, 401-555-0156. Do you want to try clearing the leaves off the grate yourself? Only if it's safe, stay out of the street.
I tried a little with a rake. The top layer comes off and then there's a wet mat underneath that doesn't budge. I'm not sticking my arm down there.
No, definitely don't. Leave that to the crew. I've got you down, and the note says clogged with leaves, flowing toward the neighbor's garage.

Perfect. Oh, and one more thing, unrelated. If you call back and it rings forever, it's not that I'm ignoring you. My wifi drops every time somebody runs the microwave, so I'm usually yelling at the router.
Okay, noted. Landline it is, then. Anything else going on out there?
That's it. Just the basin. Thanks, Kevin. Stay dry.
You too, Dominic. Somebody will get out there as soon as they can.
